Hello everyone, I'm Mun! Welcome to my channel. Today, we're going to wander through the streets of Busan together.

Busan's port first opened in 1407 as Busanpo, a key trading post during the early Joseon Dynasty connecting Korea with Japan. After isolation, it reopened to foreign trade in 1876, becoming Korea's first international port.

The population had reached about 200,000 by 1936, then swelled sharply after Korea's 1945 independence and again during the 1950-53 Korean War, as huge numbers of refugees poured into the city seeking safety and shelter.

Over the following decades, Busan's population grew from roughly 1.3 million to about 3.4 million residents today, making it South Korea's second-largest city overall by population, trailing only the capital city of Seoul.

Today the port ranks among the world's busiest container hubs, handling around 20 million TEU of cargo annually and roughly 80 percent of all South Korea's total container traffic passing through its busy docks each year.

Despite that industrial scale, Busan's regional GDP has recently dipped just below 5 percent of the national total, prompting local city leaders to pursue new efforts toward broader industrial and economic reform citywide.
